intelligence.essence: "They're not going to understand it, but it's going to feel like magic to them." People will never grasp the intelligence architecture — the scorecards, the token systems, the 100 Laws, the measurement loops. They don't need to. What they feel: visual bliss, push-button simple, everything alive, Naya just knowing. Magic = deep complexity hidden behind perfect simplicity. Understanding is not required for value. Rule: never expose the machinery. If the user has to understand how it works, we've failed the presentation layer.
